factProposals.value: Generated ideas are stored in an append-only JSON-lines log at data/ideas.jsonl; each line holds the idea's id, title, theme and status, a timestamp and an idempotency key, and logging the same idea in the same status twice adds no line.
Moderation can only produce the statuses pending, flagged or removed. No code sets an idea to approved, and nothing is published; approval is left to a human.
Idea generation sits behind an IdeaGenerator interface. Only a stub implementation exists, returning a fixed set of ideas, so a real generator can replace it later.
No external AI service is connected; the stub needs no API key and makes no network call.

decisions.statement: Build the generator as a stub first, with no API key and no network call.
decisions.rationale: The repository is public and no credential exists.

decisions.statement: An idea that is not clearly allowed is flagged for human review instead of being approved or removed.
decisions.rationale: When the rules are unsure, a person should decide; the code never approves an idea.

decisions.statement: Every generated idea is logged before moderation runs.
decisions.rationale: A crash during moderation must not lose an idea.

decisions.statement: The words depict, portray, reenact and impersonat were added to the blocklist at the project owner's request.
decisions.rationale: The project owner asked for ideas about depicting, portraying, re-enacting or impersonating to be blocked.

limitations.statement: The stub ignores the prompt and is not a real AI, so the criterion that the AI generates a list of video ideas is met only with a stub.
The 'AI generates irrelevant ideas' failure path cannot be demonstrated yet, because the stub always returns the same fixed ideas.
Moderation is keyword matching on the start of words, so it can remove harmless ideas, for example a title that uses the word 'depict' innocently.
The allowlist and blocklist cannot check religious accuracy, so human review is still needed.
The pipeline does not read statuses back from the log, so re-running it can return an idea as pending even if a human later changed its status.
There are no timeouts or retries yet, because nothing makes an external call.
The log supports one writer only; two processes writing at once are not protected against each other.
